rule.note: Alpha hairline over the ground; ramp derived from its opaque hue.

rule-strong.note: Alpha hairline over the ground; ramp derived from its opaque hue.

rule-dark.note: Alpha hairline over the ground; ramp derived from its opaque hue.

display.purpose: Hero line and color-run names, uppercase, spanning the gutters; the object may sit in front of it.

headline.purpose: Uppercase section titles (details, about); the color-run title runs at clamp(36px, 5.2vw, 88px).

title.purpose: Selected colorway name in the configurator, uppercase.

wordmark.purpose: MANGO with a clay-pebble O in the live colorway; 24px on mobile, 25.4vw in the footer.

statement.purpose: Serif section intros and soft copy; sentence case, balanced wrap.

serif-title.purpose: Detail-list headings; FAQ questions use the same voice.

body.purpose: Running text; long paragraphs cap at 52 to 60ch.

shadows.name: hairline-inset
shadows.purpose: Edge for tool buttons and the FAQ icon box; a border, not elevation.

shadows.name: nav-underline
shadows.purpose: Bottom edge of the solid nav and mobile menu.

shadows.name: swatch-ring

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Background dim behind the cart drawer.

shadows.name: clay-contact

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default curve for reveals, underlines, swatches, drawer and widget.

motion.name: line-reveal

motion.purpose: Headlines rising out of their own masks on scroll-in.

motion.name: underline-draw

motion.name: drench
motion.purpose: Color run, band and drenched button changing colorway.

motion.name: run-name
motion.purpose: Colorway names cycling in the color run.

motion.name: word-ink
motion.purpose: Manifesto inking in as it crosses the viewport.

motion.name: cart-bump
motion.purpose: Cart count when an item is added.

motion.name: clay-idle
motion.value: spin 0.22 rad/s default (x5 on tile hover), float sin(1.1t) * 0.035
motion.purpose: The object never sits fully still; colors lerp toward the target colorway.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; scroll-linked word and band effects also stop.

narrative.overview:
MANGO is a warm, gray studio ground with one thing on it: a small clay piece, rendered live in WebGL, soft and slightly lopsided. The page photographs nothing. The object does every job a product photo usually does: it fronts the hero, turns in the configurator, re-colors through the color run and sits in each collection tile. The UI around it is printed, not built. Huge tight uppercase grotesk, a soft serif speaking voice, hairline rules, square edges, and no cards, so the only volume and the only shadow on the page belong to the clay.

Color works by drenching. The neutral ground stays quiet until a colorway takes over: the color run pins a full viewport and swaps its whole field and type color through all ten colorways as you scroll, and the selected colorway also tints the wordmark's clay "O", the sliding band and the buy widget's thumbnail. A colorway is never a small accent on a white card. It owns the region it touches.

Density is editorial. Sections breathe (140px vertical padding on desktop), headlines run edge to edge, and supporting copy sits in narrow columns on a 12-column grid. Motion is slow and eased: lines rise out of their own masks, words ink in with scroll, and clay colors ease between colorways rather than snapping.
keyCharacteristics: One live 3D clay object as the only imagery; matte, grained, hand-irregular, never glossy.
Warm studio-gray paper ground with brown-black ink; one dark section for contrast.
Ten colorways, each a four-part set (base, top, field, ink) that drenches whole regions.
Schibsted Grotesk set huge, uppercase and tight; Young Serif for the soft human voice.
Hairline rules and inset 1px strokes instead of borders, cards or elevation.
Square UI chrome; roundness belongs to the clay and its swatch portraits.

rules.name: The Drench Rule
rules.body: A colorway appears as a whole field with its own ink on top, or as clay. It never appears as a small accent chip on the neutral ground (the round swatch, which is a portrait of the clay, is the one exception).

rules.name: The Quartet Rule
rules.body: Base, top, field and ink travel together. Never set one colorway's ink on another colorway's field.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Grotesk shouts in uppercase; the serif speaks in sentence case. Never set Young Serif in uppercase, never set a full sentence of body copy in the display style.

rules.name: The Edge-to-Edge Rule
rules.body: Display type is sized in viewport units so it spans the gutters; the live object is allowed to sit in front of it.

rules.name: The Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: The clay casts the only shadows. UI surfaces separate by tone (Paper, Paper Raised, Kiln Dark) and hairlines, never by elevation.

rules.name: The Square Chrome Rule
rules.body: If it is interface, it has square corners. If it is clay, or a picture of clay, it is round and irregular.

dos: Do render the product only as the live clay object (or its flat glyph in small UI); let it overlap display type.
Do use a colorway as a full field with its own ink (The Drench Rule), cross-fading over 0.8s with the ease-in-out curve when it changes.
Do set headlines in Schibsted Grotesk 560, uppercase, -0.04em, sized in viewport units to span the gutters.
Do give every human-sounding sentence to Young Serif in sentence case.
Do separate content with 1px hairlines (Hairline or Hairline Strong) and tonal grounds.
Do keep all interface corners square (0px) and icons in the single 1.5-stroke, square-cap family.
Do reveal headlines line by line from their own masks (1.15s, 85ms stagger) and honor reduced motion by collapsing all durations.
Do use tabular numerals for prices, counts and request numbers.
donts: Don't add drop shadows or elevation to UI; the clay casts the only shadows.
Don't put content in rounded cards or pastel-gradient tiles; the build has no cards.
Don't use photographs, downloaded models or pre-rendered images of the object.
Don't make the clay glossy, smooth or perfectly symmetric; keep it matte and irregular.
Don't mix one colorway's ink with another colorway's field (The Quartet Rule).
Don't set Young Serif in uppercase, or body paragraphs in the display style.
Don't use pure black or pure white as the page ground or text color at rest; use Studio Ink and Studio Paper.
